detail:
MedlinePlus describes osteoporosis management as aimed at slowing bone loss, preserving bone strength, relieving symptoms, and preventing fractures. Sources describe adequate calcium and vitamin D intake, regular weight-bearing and muscle-strengthening activity, limiting alcohol, and not smoking as lifestyle foundations of care plans. Therapists and clinicians typically build activity programs around weight-bearing exercise and balance and posture work intended in part to reduce fall risk, and fall-prevention measures at home are described as part of many care plans.

MedlinePlus notes that clinicians may prescribe medicine classes such as bisphosphonates, hormone-related therapies, and other bone-active agents for people at higher fracture risk, selecting among them based on sex, fracture history, bone density, and other health conditions. Follow-up usually includes repeat bone density testing at intervals a clinician sets, monitoring for fractures and height changes, and review of calcium, vitamin D, and medicines that can affect bone. Sources present treatment as long-term management rather than a cure, since bone loss can resume when therapy stops.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about managing osteoporosis and preventing fractures.
summary: MedlinePlus describes osteoporosis management aimed at slowing bone loss and preventing fractures, combining calcium and vitamin D, weight-bearing activity, and fall prevention with bone-active medicine classes for higher-risk patients.
takeaways: care plans combine nutrition, weight-bearing activity, and fall prevention
bone-active medicine classes are selected by fracture risk and health history
never start, stop, or change medicines without your doctor
title: Osteoporosis: protecting bone strength and preventing fractures day to day
